title.narrative: SWE-2011-67 Social accountability of the local state in China (People's Republic of)
SWE-2011-67 Social accountability of the local state in China (People's Republic of)

description.narrative: The project will study how citizens can hold local officials and authorities accountable in China (People's Republic of). The concept social accountability is used to analyze non-electoral forms of accountability such as media, internet, hearings and citizen evaluations. We will test five hypotheses on the conditions when social accountability is likely to be successful. The outcome is measured as (1) answerability (2) sanctions, and (3) legal rights attainment. The city of Hangzhou will constitute a crucial case where the circumstances are benign. We will use process tracing to examine events where citizens are claiming their rights towards authorities. Through interviews with activists and officials and analysis of media we will map the mechanisms resulting in successful social accountability. The theoretical contribution is a test of the concept social accountability in an authoritarian political context.
